title: Intel CEO says Chinese frontier AI model adoption has been 'very fast'
source_used: The Economic Times (carrying Reuters' text; Reuters page returned HTTP 401)
key_facts: Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said on Monday 12 Oct 2026 that the token costs of Chinese frontier AI models have been lower and that their adoption has been 'very fast'.
He spoke at a panel organised by the lender DBS.
He said the performance of Chinese models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM is 'good enough'.
He said 'I'm a strong believer of open source, that's the best way to drive efficiency' and that markets will decide which models benefit different uses most.
He added that quantum computing could become mainstream in the next three to five years and that software will help drive efficient use of the infrastructure required.
The text gives no figures for the cost gap or the adoption rate.
quote_evidence: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Monday that the token costs of Chinese frontier AI models have been lower and adoption has been "very fast".
At a panel organised by lender DBS on Monday, Tan said the performances of Chinese models, such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, are "good enough".
"I'm a strong believer of open source, that's the best way to drive efficiency," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: The chief of a major US chip maker says Chinese AI models are cheaper to run, good enough and quickly adopted.
